Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Pakistan's reply. Dasun Shanaka leads his troops out onto the park. It will be the left-hand, right-hand combination of Saim Ayub and Sahibzada Farhan to open the innings for the visiting side. Nuwan Thushara will open the attack for Sri Lanka. Farhan to face the first ball. A slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The two-paced nature of the surface and the way the two Pakistani leg-spinners got purchase from it is something Sri Lanka can cling to for hope. That said, given the rain around, parts of the park beyond the fence are still wet, and whenever the ball has come back from there, the bowlers have had to wipe it dry. That will make life tough for the spinners. As for Pakistan, they will be confident enough to gun down this total and will be after a steady start that puts them in good stead for the rest of the chase. Back in a bit for the second essay.

Janith Liyanage brought some stability to the home side, first through his partnership with Charith Asalanka and then with Wanindu Hasaranga. He had his share of luck, though, having been dropped twice, on 4 and 21, with the first chance being the easier one, but Sahibzada Farhan could not cling on. The stand with Hasaranga gave the momentum the hosts were in search of, but once that partnership was broken, it did not take long for the innings to taper off. From being 127/6, Sri Lanka were folded for 128, losing 4 wickets for just one run.

Pakistan opted to make first use of the surface and the moisture from the rain that had been around Dambulla. While the movement off the deck or through the air was not a lot, it was the two-paced nature of the surface that messed with the batters' timing early on. That led to the downfall of the two Lankan openers. After the pacers, it were the spinners who tightened the screws in the middle phase. Shadab Khan bowled as if he had never been out of the side, while it was business as usual for Abrar Ahmed. Their combined figures read 8-0-50-5 with Abrar picking 3 wickets.

Well, it all fizzled out for Sri Lanka towards the back end. The home side will be disappointed with their effort. While there were brief sparks of promise, they could never really hit the top gear. A job well done from Pakistan after electing to bowl first, and while there is still work left to be done, they will be pleased with how it panned out for them in the field.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Faheem Ashraf to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shot! It's a gift from Ashraf. He goes short and takes the pace off as well. Around middle and it sits up nicely for the batter. Mendis rides the bounce and pulls it superbly in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Faheem Ashraf to Kusal Mendis, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it on a length and outside off, Kusal drives it on the up, finds good timing too but again fails to pierce the gap on the off side. Finds point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Faheem Ashraf to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Better from Faheem. Serves it on a length and close to off, Dhananjaya de Silva stays back and taps it towards third man for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Faheem Ashraf to Dhananjaya de Silva, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Bang! This is some shot from Dhananjaya de Silva. Faheem delivers a seam-up delivery, around off and on a fuller length. De Silva goes across the line and swings it with good connection over mid-wicket, for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Faheem Ashraf to Dhananjaya de Silva, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: We're done and dusted with 5 overs now. Time for the first bowling change of the night. No spin just yet. Faheem Ashraf comes into the attack, replacing Mohammad Wasim.
Angled in and then it straightens off the deck, on a short of a good length. Dhananjaya de Silva is squared up in defence and the ball squirts off an outside edge, wide of point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Salman Mirza to Dhananjaya de Silva, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off, into the deck, over off, Kusal nudges it in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Salman Mirza to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...but safe! From around the wicket for the right-hander, on a back of a length. Dhananjaya is tempted by the width on offer and he throws his hands at it. Gets a thickish outside edge but luckily for him, it does not carry all the way to deep third. Mohammad Wasim collects it on the bounce. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Salman Mirza to Dhananjaya de Silva, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another ball that is a bit too short and equally wide, Kusal reaches out for the cut but gets it right off the toe end and it goes behind point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Salman Mirza to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely put away! Mirza tries to run it across the right-hander but ends up offering too much width and errs in length as well. A bit too short, Mendis reaches out and cuts it past point for a four.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Salman Mirza to Kusal Mendis, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Mirza bashes the hard length, outside off, de Silva drags the pull off the toe end of the blade, wide of mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Salman Mirza to Dhananjaya de Silva, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: It's been a good start from Pakistan and Salman Agha has decided to give Salman Mirza his third over.
Banged in short, over off, Kusal Mendis ducks under it. End of a successful over for Wasim. Just 2 runs and a wicket off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Mohammad Wasim to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: At the stumps, on a length, Dhananjaya wrists it from the crease, wide of mid-wicket for a single to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Mohammad Wasim to Dhananjaya de Silva, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slightly fuller, on off, de Silva taps it off the front foot to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Mohammad Wasim to Dhananjaya de Silva, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length, on off, Dhananjaya de Silva hangs back to defend.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Mohammad Wasim to Dhananjaya de Silva, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It's a big blow to Sri Lanka and Dhananjaya de Silva has been sent to partner Mendis in the middle. A comeback game for Dhananjaya in T20Is, he last played in this format was June 16, 2024.

OUT! CAUGHT! Taken on the second attempt by Mohammad Nawaz. Pathum Nissanka looks at the bottom half of his bat as he trudges off. Wasim slams the surface, over middle and leg. Nissanka has a big swipe across the line but fails to get the desired connection. Gets it only as far as deep square leg, where Nawaz gets around to his left. The ball hits his palm and pops out, but the fielder is alert enough to complete the catch on the second go.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Nawaz b Mohammad Wasim
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Mohammad Wasim to Pathum Nissanka, OUT! c Mohammad Nawaz b Mohammad Wasim.

Commentary.Commentary: Shaping back a bit, full and on off. Mendis plays the drive in front of his body and the ball goes a bit uppishly between cover and mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Mohammad Wasim to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slight hold up in play. There is a light glowing right above the sightscreen. That's bothering Kusal Mendis. The issue is fixed ,and here we go...

Excellent delivery. Salman gets this delivery to jag away a bit from around off. On a length and Mendis tries to defend from the crease. But it takes the outer edge and squirts down to third man for a single. End of a successful over from Mirza.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Salman Mirza to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the channel outside off, on a length and angling away, Mendis allows it through to the keeper. Watchful.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Salman Mirza to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good timing but not so good placement. Full and angling away, outside off, Mendis drives well but finds the fielder at point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Salman Mirza to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around middle and off, on back of a length, Kusal defends off the back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Salman Mirza to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Early setback for Sri Lanka has brought Kusal Mendis in the middle, at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! A soft and rather disappointing end for Kamil Mishara. Salman Mirza goes full around middle and the pitch just grips a touch. Mishara leans into the drive, plays it too early and tries to lift it, but only manages a meek chip. The ball balloons invitingly in front of mid off, where Salman Agha strolls in and snaffles it with a smile. A three-ball duck for Mishara, as the two Salmans combine to do the damage.
Commentary.Howout: c Salman Agha b Salman Mirza
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Salman Mirza to Kamil Mishara, OUT! c Salman Agha b Salman Mirza.

Commentary.Commentary: Begins with a short ball around middle, Pathum is hurried into the shot and pulls it without much conviction behind square leg. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Salman Mirza to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Will Salman Agha make a change? The answer is no. Mirza to continue. The slip fielder has disappeared now.
Wasim rushes the batter with his pace. Around middle and Kamil somehow keeps it out towards mid-wicket. A good over from Wasim.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Mohammad Wasim to Kamil Mishara, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Closer to the off stump, on a back of a length, Pathum taps it in front of mid on and turns the strike over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Mohammad Wasim to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Width offered and Nissanka cashes in! This is on a short of a length, outside off. Fast hands from Pathum as he cuts it fine of the man at deep backward point for a four. The outfield is lightning quick despite all the rain.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Mohammad Wasim to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Not in control but safe! Wasim bends his back and digs it in short, around the right shoulder. Pathum tries to take the short ball on but the ball skids through and also gets big on the batter. It comes off the splice of the bat and lobs over Mishara at the non-striker's end, well in front of the man at mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Mohammad Wasim to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the fuller side, a bit of nip back into the right-hander, on the off stump. Pathum brings his bat out in front and stabs it down the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Mohammad Wasim to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it on a good length, in the corridor, Pathum Nissanka waits back, covers the line and defends it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Mohammad Wasim to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mohammad Wasim to steam in from the other end. One slip in place for him as well. We've not seen too much movement so far. Can Wasim make the ball talk?
A touch short and in line of the stumps, Pathum stays back and turns it behind square leg. They cross for a run and close the first over. 7 coming off it!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Salman Mirza to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Full and darted onto the pads. Mishara misses out on the tickle as he is beaten for pace. A leg bye is sneaked in as the ball dribbles between short fine leg and the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Salman Mirza to Kamil Mishara, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Off-cutter from Mirza at 127 kph, fuller and around off. Pathum Nissanka pushes out in front of his body and does not pick the slower one. The ball goes off the outer half down to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Salman Mirza to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good comeback! Mirza drags the length back and gets the ball to jag back into the right-hander. Nissanka hops and hurriedly drops his bat down on the ball and it rolls beside him on the leg side. Pathum thinks of stealing a run, takes a step forward as the bowler rushes forward. Kamil Mishara sends his partner back.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Salman Mirza to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Pathum Nissanka and Sri Lanka are away! This is pushed across the right-hander, on a fuller length. Not a lot of foot movement from Nissanka. He plays the drive on the up between cover and mid off for the first boundary of the contest.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Salman Mirza to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: The batter is not ready and pulls out as the bowler is about to deliver. Strong wind, perhaps, disturbed Pathum Nissanka. Reload.
Mirza is right on the money! Steams in from over the wicket and serves it full, attacking the stumps. A hint of shape back into the right-hander. Nissanka watchfully blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Salman Mirza to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre match formalities, it is now time to play. The Pakistan players get into a huddle before spreading across the field as a decent crowd settles in for the contest. Pathum Nissanka and Kamil Mishara stride out to open for Sri Lanka. Salman Mirza, the left-arm pacer, is to begin proceedings. One slip in place. Here we go...
The players from both sides have lined up in the middle for their respective national anthems. Pakistan's first, followed by Sri Lanka's...

PITCH REPORT - Jon Kent, the South African, is near the deck. He reports that this is pitch number five, with equidistant square boundaries measuring 68 metres. Shares that there is a fair bit of moisture beneath a good grass covering, and he believes the surface could be a bit two-paced. Informs that the average first-innings score here is around 164, and overall, it looks like a pitch that will offer something for everyone.

Dasun Shanaka, the Sri Lankan skipper, says the pitch looks good for batting. He also notes that it is under cover but expects a high-scoring contest, as is typical of a Dambulla surface. Informs that their XI has 7 batters, including 4 all-rounders. He adds that it is a good opportunity for the players to showcase their skills. Shanaka mentions that the team is feeling confident, everyone is keen to express themselves, and he hopes they deliver the goods.

The captain of Pakistan, Salman Agha, says the decision to bowl first was influenced by the surface having been under covers, and they want to make use of any moisture on offer early on. Informs that Shadab Khan is back in the side, and they have a very balanced unit, with 8 batting options and 6-7 bowling options at their disposal. Shares that everyone is excited in the camp with the World Cup coming up. Adds that some players are preparing for their first World Cup, while some have been part of previous editions.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kamil Mishara, Kusal Mendis (WK), Dhananjaya de Silva, Charith Asalanka, Dasun Shanaka (C), Janith Liyanage, Wanindu Hasaranga, Maheesh Theekshana, Dushmantha Chameera and Nuwan Thushara.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Saim Ayub, Sahibzada Farhan, Salman Agha (C), Fakhar Zaman, Usman Khan (WK), Shadab Khan, Mohammad Nawaz, Faheem Ashraf, Mohammad Wasim, Salman Mirza and Abrar Ahmed.
Toss - Up goes the coin, and down comes the verdict in favour of the visiting side. PAKISTAN ELECT TO FIELD! Please wait as we gather the details of the playing XIs for both sides.

There has been rain around Dambulla, with teams unable to train on the eve of the game, and even the trophy unveiling had to take place indoors. That said, conditions have improved since, and let's hope we get an uninterrupted contest. With rain in the lead-up and the surface being under covers, it looks very much a no-brainer for the captain winning the toss to bowl first. Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

As for Pakistan, with all their World Cup matches set to be played in Sri Lanka, this series takes on added importance. It offers a valuable chance to adapt to local conditions and fine-tune combinations ahead of the tournament. A home series against Australia before the World Cup is also in the pipeline, with dates yet to be confirmed. So far, the team under the partnership of Mike Hesson and Salman Agha has yet to fire on all cylinders or present itself as a genuine world-beating unit. The squad announcement was headlined by the return of all-rounder Shadab Khan, who has made impactful contributions in the ongoing Big Bash League and adds balance and experience to the side. Pakistan will be without Babar Azam and Haris Rauf for this series, while Shaheen Afridi, who was also featuring in the BBL, saw his stint cut short by a knee injury.

Three games against Pakistan and another three later this month when England visit, that’s all Sri Lanka have left before the World Cup. In case you missed it, there has been a change in leadership for the island nation in this format. During the tri-series in Pakistan, Dasun Shanaka took over the captaincy from Charith Asalanka due to illness, and Shanaka will continue to lead the side heading into the global event. Asalanka will feature in this series, and he will be keen to rediscover his best form after an underwhelming 2025. The story of Sri Lanka’s 2025 campaign was their heavy reliance on Pathum Nissanka at the top of the order, while with the ball, consistency remained a concern. The fast bowlers, in particular, will be keen to draw on the vast experience of Lasith Malinga, who has been roped in as a fast-bowling consultant.

Hello and welcome, everyone! With exactly a month to go before the T20 World Cup, teams are in the final stages of their preparations for the mega event. The two sides that clashed in their final game of 2025 meet again to usher in the new year, as Sri Lanka host Pakistan in a three-match T20I series. All three games will be played at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium, and while Dambulla will not host any World Cup fixtures, the conditions are expected to be not too different from what teams will encounter in Colombo and Pallekele.
... MATCH DAY ...

With exactly a month to go before the T20 World Cup 2026 gets underway, co-hosted by Sri Lanka and India, the road to the global showpiece gathers real momentum as Sri Lanka and Pakistan face off in the 1st T20I of the three-match series at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium, a venue that often tests both skill and adaptability. For Sri Lanka, this series is a crucial checkpoint in their World Cup build-up, especially at home, where conditions could mirror what awaits them later on. Led by Dasun Shanaka, the hosts boast a balanced squad that blends experience with versatility. The batting unit is expected to be anchored by the consistency of Pathum Nissanka at the top, with Kusal Mendis and Kusal Perera providing stability and intent through the middle, while Charith Asalanka and Dhananjaya de Silva offer the flexibility to either rebuild or accelerate depending on the situation. Kamindu Mendis and Janith Liyanage add depth, ensuring Sri Lanka are not overly reliant on one phase of the innings. Their biggest strength, however, lies in their bowling variety, particularly on spin-friendly surfaces, with Dunith Wellalage and Maheesh Theekshana capable of controlling the middle overs and creating constant pressure, complemented by Wanindu Hasaranga's all-round value. In the pace department, Matheesha Pathirana's unique death-over skills, along with the experience of Dushmantha Chameera and the control of Nuwan Thushara, give Sri Lanka plenty of options across phases, making them a well-rounded unit on familiar turf. Pakistan, meanwhile, arrive with a fresh-looking squad under the leadership of Salman Agha, missing several marquee names such as Babar Azam, Haris Rauf and Hasan Ali, who have not been named even in the preliminary World Cup squad, while Shaheen Afridi continues his rehabilitation from a knee injury suffered during the BBL. Despite those absences, Pakistan still possess plenty of intrigue and depth, with this series offering a golden opportunity for fringe players to stake a claim ahead of the World Cup. Shadab Khan's inclusion is a major boost after his impressive all-round displays for the Thunder in the BBL, while Faheem Ashraf comes in brimming with confidence after showing his bowling prowess in the ongoing BPL with 11 wickets in just three games. Mohammad Nawaz adds further balance with his all-round skills and arrives in terrific recent form, capable of influencing games both with his left-arm spin and his clean hitting down the order. The batting will look to players like Fakhar Zaman for experience and firepower, with Saim Ayub, Sahibzada Farhan and Usman Khan eager to make their mark at the top. Among the newer faces, Khawaja Nafay is one to watch with the bat, having shown composure and stroke-play that could translate well at this level. With the ball, Pakistan have genuine pace through Naseem Shah and Mohammad Wasim, complemented by the guile of Abrar Ahmed, while Usman Tariq adds control and confidence, coming in with some tremendous form. Tariq has not gone wicketless in T20s since March 2025, picking up 44 wickets in 21 innings at a stunning average of 13.45. With selection calls, combinations and World Cup roles very much under the spotlight, this opening encounter promises a fascinating contest where preparation meets opportunity and every performance could carry significance far beyond this series.
